criteria.text: `outlets.json` exists at repo root with exactly the five entries and field values from the issue body, unmodified (`domain`, `lean`, `basis`, `note`, `sources` byte-identical) — checked by a test that deep-equals the imported file against a literal copy of the issue's JSON.

A single `domain=<host>` query, on every route that accepts it, behaves identically to pre-issue behavior — `test/graph.test.ts:58-61` (`filters by source and by domain`), `test/graph.test.ts:266-276` (rising's AC9), `test/docs.test.ts:47-48` (AC7) pass unmodified.

`domain=a,b` matches docs whose domain is any listed value, dedupes repeated tokens, and falls back to `all` when every token is invalid — new test, mirroring `parseSourceList`'s existing test coverage.
A new `lean` parser accepts comma-separated `left`/`right`/`center`, drops unknown tokens silently, and falls back to `all` when nothing valid survives.

`lean=right` (domain unset) scopes to every outlets.json domain labeled `right` (`oantagonista.com.br`, `crusoe.com.br`) and no others; a doc on an unlabeled domain (e.g. `example.org`) never appears under any `lean` value, including when its own docs otherwise clearly dominate the window.
`domain=<x>&lean=<y>` intersects: a domain that satisfies `domain` but not `lean` (or vice versa) is excluded; the case where the intersection is empty returns zero docs, not an error, not `all`.
`GET /api/people/:id/sources` now actually filters by `q.domain` (regression test proves a `domain=` param changes the returned rows, where before it was silently ignored).

`graphFor`, `docsFor`, `risingFor` responses carry a top-level `outlets: {domain,lean,basis}[]`, empty when `lean` is unset/`all`, populated with the matched outlets.json entries when `lean` narrows the scope.

`GET /api/people/:id/sources` rows carry `lean`/`basis` (`null` when the row's domain is absent from `outlets.json`), present on every row regardless of whether `lean` was passed, and the route's top-level response stays a bare array.
`GET /api/people/:id/timeline` response stays a bare `{bucket_start,count}[]` array (no `outlets` field, no wrapper) while still honoring `lean` for which docs count toward each bucket.
No existing pinned `pmi`/`tone`/`count` literal in `graph.test.ts`, `signature*.test.ts`, `timeline*.test.ts`, `docs.test.ts`, `rising`-related tests changes.
